```{r}
## Load packages needed for the analysis
library(readr) 
library(dplyr)      
library(ggplot2)    
library(tidyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(stargazer)
library(janitor)
```

```{r}
## Load the cleaned Steam dataset with the new genre variable added
Steam <- read_csv('/Users/vickywu/Documents/ECO 590 Data Analytics/final-project-SakurairoKaden/steam_games_with_genres.csv')
```

```{r}
## Clean and create variables
Steam <- Steam %>%
  mutate(
    ## Converting the positive review score variable into numeric format
    positive_ratio = as.numeric(positive_ratio),

    ## Converting release year into numeric format
    release_year = as.numeric(release_year),

    ## Converting price into numeric format
    price = as.numeric(price),

    ## Converting total number of reviews into numeric format
    total_reviews = as.numeric(total_reviews),

    ## Converting positive review count into numeric format
    positive = as.numeric(positive),

    ## Converting negative review count into numeric format
    negative = as.numeric(negative),

    ## Create a logged version of total reviews
    log_total_reviews = log1p(total_reviews),

    ## Create release period groups based on release year
    release_period = case_when(
      release_year < 2010 ~ "Before 2010",
      release_year >= 2010 & release_year <= 2014 ~ "2010-2014",
      release_year >= 2015 & release_year <= 2019 ~ "2015-2019",
      release_year >= 2020 ~ "2020-2026",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_))
```

```{r}
## Creating genre variables
Steam <- Steam %>%
  mutate(
    primary_genre = str_split(genres, ", ", simplify = TRUE)[,1])

## Create dummy variables for every genre
## Unknown is removed because it is not an actual genre
Steam_Genre_Dummies <- Steam %>%
  filter(!is.na(genres), genres != "Unknown") %>%
  select(appid, genres) %>%
  separate_rows(genres, sep = ", ") %>%
  mutate(
    genres = str_trim(genres),

    ## Translate non-English genre names into English I had AI to help get all non English names 
    genres = case_when(
      genres %in% c("Acción", "Ação", "Экшены", "动作") ~ "Action",
      genres %in% c("Aventura", "Abenteuer", "Приключенческие игры") ~ "Adventure",
      genres %in% c("Инди") ~ "Indie",
      genres %in% c("Казуальные игры") ~ "Casual",
      genres %in% c("Simuladores", "Симуляторы", "Simulationen") ~ "Simulation",
      genres %in% c("Strategie") ~ "Strategy",
      genres %in% c("Rol") ~ "RPG",
      genres %in% c("Ранний доступ") ~ "Early Access",
      TRUE ~ genres),

    genre_value = 1) %>%

  ## Combine duplicate genres for the same game
  group_by(appid, genres) %>%
  summarise(
    genre_value = max(genre_value),
    .groups = "drop") %>%

  ## Turn each genre into its own column
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = genres,
    values_from = genre_value,
    values_fill = 0,
    names_prefix = "genre_") %>%
  clean_names()

## Add the genre dummy variables back into the main Steam dataset
## This removes old genre columns first in case the code was already run
Steam <- Steam %>%
  select(-matches("^genre_")) %>%
  left_join(Steam_Genre_Dummies, by = "appid")
```

```{r}
## Show all columns in the Steam dataset that are genre dummy variables
names(Steam)[grepl("genre_", names(Steam))]
```


```{r}
## Summary information about the dataset to show how many observations are available before the regressions
cat("Total rows in dataset:", nrow(Steam), "\n")
cat("Games with review score:", sum(!is.na(Steam$positive_ratio)), "\n")
cat("Games with release year:", sum(!is.na(Steam$release_year)), "\n")
cat("Games with price:", sum(!is.na(Steam$price)), "\n")
cat("Games with total reviews:", sum(!is.na(Steam$total_reviews)), "\n")
cat("Games with genre information:", sum(!is.na(Steam$genres) & Steam$genres != "Unknown"), "\n")
cat("Games with Unknown genre:", sum(Steam$genres == "Unknown", na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
```

```{r}
## Count how many games are in each genre
genre_columns <- names(Steam)[grepl("^genre_", names(Steam))] ## Find all columns that start with "genre_"

## Create a table that counts how many games belong to each genre
genre_counts <- Steam %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(genre_columns), ~sum(.x == 1, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "Genre",
    values_to = "Number_of_Games") %>%
  arrange(desc(Number_of_Games))

## Print the genre count table
print(genre_counts)
```


```{r}
## Regression Model 1: Release Year

## Create a regression dataset only for Model 1 with missing values is excluded
Steam_Reg1 <- Steam %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(positive_ratio),
    !is.na(release_year),
    !is.na(price),
    !is.na(log_total_reviews))

## Show how many rows are used in Model 1
cat("Rows available for Model 1:", nrow(Steam_Reg1), "\n")

## Run the regression model with main variable of interest release_year to tests whether newer games have higher or lower review scores
Reg1 <- lm(positive_ratio ~ release_year + price + log_total_reviews,
           data = Steam_Reg1)

## Display the results for Model 1
summary(Reg1)
```

```{r}

## Regression Model 2: Release Period

## Create a regression dataset only for Model 2 and missing values is excluded
Steam_Reg2 <- Steam %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(positive_ratio),
    !is.na(release_period),
    !is.na(price),
    !is.na(log_total_reviews))

## Set the order of the release period categories, using Before 2010 as the comparison/reference group
## So other periods will be compared against games released before 2010
Steam_Reg2$release_period <- factor(
  Steam_Reg2$release_period,
  levels = c("Before 2010", "2010-2014", "2015-2019", "2020-2026"))

## Show how many rows are used in Model 2
cat("Rows available for Model 2:", nrow(Steam_Reg2), "\n")

## Run the regression model to compares review scores across different release periods
Reg2 <- lm(positive_ratio ~ release_period + price + log_total_reviews,
           data = Steam_Reg2)

## Display the results for Model 2
summary(Reg2)
```

```{r}
## Regression Model 3: Genre Model

## Find all genre dummy variables created earlier
genre_columns <- names(Steam)[grepl("^genre_", names(Steam))]

## Create a regression dataset only for Model 3 with missing values excluded
## Unknown genres are excluded because Unknown is not an actual genre
Steam_Reg3 <- Steam %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(positive_ratio),
    !is.na(release_year),
    !is.na(price),
    !is.na(log_total_reviews),
    !is.na(genres),
    genres != "Unknown")

## Show how many rows are used in Model 3
cat("Rows available for Model 3:", nrow(Steam_Reg3), "\n")

## Create the regression formula using all genre variables
Reg3_Formula <- as.formula(
  paste(
    "positive_ratio ~ release_year + price + log_total_reviews +",
    paste(genre_columns, collapse = " + ")))

## Run the regression model
Reg3 <- lm(Reg3_Formula, data = Steam_Reg3)

## Display the results for Model 3
summary(Reg3)
```

```{r regression-table, results='asis', echo=FALSE}

## Find all genre dummy variables used in Model 3
genre_columns <- names(Steam)[grepl("^genre_", names(Steam))]

## Create cleaner genre labels for the regression table
genre_labels <- genre_columns %>% 
  str_replace("^genre_", "") %>%    ## Remove the "genre_" part from each variable name
  str_replace_all("_", " ") %>%     ## Replace underscores with spaces
  str_to_title() %>%                ## Capitalize the first letter of each word
  paste("Game")                     ## Add the word "Game" to the end of each label

## Create a clean regression table from the three regression models
stargazer(Reg1, Reg2, Reg3,
          type = "html",
          title = "Steam Games: What Drives Positive Review Ratios?",
          column.labels = c("Age of Game", "Release Period", "Genre Model"),
          dep.var.labels.include = FALSE,
          dep.var.caption = "",
          covariate.labels = c(
            "Age of Game",
            "Price (USD)",
            "Log Total Reviews",
            "Release Period: 2010-2014",
            "Release Period: 2015-2019",
            "Release Period: 2020-2026",
            genre_labels),
          omit.stat = c("f", "ser"),
          digits = 4,
          star.cutoffs = c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001),
          notes = "Data: Steam API variables. Standard errors in parentheses.",
          notes.align = "c",
          no.space = TRUE)     #remove extra blank spacing between rows in the regression table.
```
